title: Hadamard Three-Lines Lemma: Log-Convexity on Complex Strips
description: Formalizes the Hadamard three-lines lemma for complex analysis: if f is bounded and analytic on the strip 0 ≤ Re(z) ≤ 1, then log M(x) is convex where M(x) = sup_y ‖f(x+iy)‖. The bound M(θ) ≤ M(0)^{1-θ} M(1)^θ is the key lemma for the Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem. 1 axiom for maximum modulus principle on strips. 23 theorems.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: maximum_modulus_strip (MMP applied to the vertical strip).

overview.historicalContext: Hadamard (1896) proved log M(x) is convex. This lemma is the key tool for proving the Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem (1926-1927).
overview.problemStatement: Prove Hadamard's three-lines lemma from the maximum modulus principle.
overview.proofStrategy: Define closed/open strips; prove boundary inclusions; derive log-convexity from MMP on strips via 1 axiom.
